about: Every wire and stored shape: its id, its owning context, its schema, the one codec file that may write it, and the command that checks it. coax/web/tool.sh wire-check holds the tree to this file. How to add a row: proto/README.md, "Register a wire shape". Plan: docs/protocol/2026-11-11-compliance-plan.md.

Bounded email-account transcripts. Uses the existing gateway codec for inference; no synthetic authenticators or legacy admin grant.
Read-only account-owned saved conversations for email L1 sessions; existing admin and write gates unchanged.

Read-only native Spark observation: status 0 loading, 1 available, 2 missing seed, 3 locked, 4 unreadable seed, 5 unavailable. Sats is -1 except for a successful supply-bounded Bitcoin balance. No seed or SDK error text crosses the bridge.
Signed CNU1 envelope and bounded manifest for the embedded WebKit/Wasm starter. SDK signature verification precedes the shared Coax decoder; stored selectors retain the same signed envelope.

Everglade's session text frames, hand-packed (30 Hz). Page and room load the same codec file; since E3b (#13364) that holds e xp, e level, e rc, e wm, e mend, e pburn, e pgone, g, v, w, L, V, X and the K reader too.

Everglade's session frames in binary (#13278), spoken on wire 7 by a page whose hello sets WIRE_HELLO_BINARY: one table of every frame and entry (opcode, fields, units, bits) and the one encoder and decoder that read it. The profile and its golden bytes are written from the table. Wire 7's text is the same table's other form (wt_bin, wt_text).
Everglade's additive J1 mounted-joust input frame (#13244). Page and room load the same codec file.
Everglade II Wild Companion: M1 SEQ FORM SLOT, m1 SEQ FORM, r SEQ familiar. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II Find Familiar: M3 SEQ FORM SLOT SPIRIT, m3 SEQ STATUS. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar pocket, recall and release: M4 SEQ ORDER, m4 SEQ ORDER. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar step: M5 SEQ, m5 SEQ. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar touch Cure Wounds: M6 SEQ SEAT, m6 SEQ. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar senses: M7 SEQ, m7 SEQ, m8 MODE. The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).
Everglade II familiar snapshot m2 TICK COUNT [OWNER FORM X Z HP MAX].... The room reads and writes it through this file; the page still has its own code (#13244, #13245).

Everglade II Healer's Kit before wire 7: U1 SEQ, u1 SEQ LEFT, r SEQ kit. The room still reads U1 and writes u1 with it for a wire 6 page, behind the previous wire's hooks (everglade/server/wire-prev.coax, #13398); since wire 7 the ask and the answer are everglade2-familiar-v2's (#13245); docs/protocol/everglade-healers-kit-v1.md.

Everglade II's familiars and Healer's Kit since wire 7 (#13276, #13245): each request an E kind (9 to 15), each answer an e entry of D told to the asker (e fam, e fam-cast, e kit), the familiar itself a row (WK_FAMILIAR, everglade-session-v7). One codec: the page writes the requests and reads the answers with it, the room reads and writes with it; docs/protocol/everglade-familiar-v2.md.

Everglade II riding in wire 7 (#13268): a mount is a row (WK_MOUNT, everglade-session-v7), each ask an E kind (20 mount, 21 get down, 22 land), the answer an e entry of D told to the asker (e ride SEQ CODE MOUNT). One codec: the page writes the asks and reads the answers and rows with it, the room reads and writes with it; docs/protocol/everglade-riding-v1.md.

Everglade II's Archery Range (#13507): the room's word on each of an archer's arrows on the range (e range ID MODE CM POINTS FACE), an e entry of D told to the archer alone, and the ask to clear the tally (E kind 23). An arrow in a face ends as a stuck arrow (aethyr-projectile-v1) whose BODY is the face. One codec: the room writes the answers and reads the ask, the page reads the answers and writes the ask; docs/protocol/everglade-range-v1.md. #13519: E kind 24 (FOOT, HORSE or DRAGON on riding's rules, answered as e ride), RESET also back to the line, e tally (the lasting tally from the character's record), and the page's words to its pane (pane HERE MODE RUN, e range, e tally; presses as message 740).

EDF1: Everglade II's dragon frames as one file beside its pack (#13519), since the browser's pack reader holds the whole pack image in 64 MiB and the image is within 4.2 MB of that, less than the frames need as pack meshes. The triangles' corners are held once as vertex numbers, then each frame's vertices. The page fetches it as an optional data asset after its world is up, admits it with edf_read, copies it into its baked-clips store past the bakes and draws each frame without an index buffer. One codec: dragon_frames.coax writes it and the page reads it.

The relay room's own frames (#13245): y SEAT N T [G], j SEAT, l SEAT, m SEAT TEXT, the clock ping t MS and its pong t MS T. The room (coax/web/room/room-relay.coax) writes them with this file and every page in a relay room reads them with it: everglade/client/net.coax, apps/openagents-web/old/v1/everglade-net.coax, lockroom.coax and oneshot.coax; docs/protocol/room-relay-v2.md. The rooms list JSON (rm_rooms) is not in it.
Everglade II's path guard (g2, g3) and monsters (h2, h3). The room writes them and the page reads them through this file (#13246); docs/protocol/everglade-guard-monsters-v2.md.

A previous wire (#13398): what a wire 7 room writes a seat whose hello said wire 5 in place of the monsters' and the guard's rows and entries (g2 g3 h2 h3, as production's 01bdb405f0 reads them). Kept while production's page speaks wire 5 (WIRE_LIVE); deleted with its writers by the first change after production moves past it; docs/protocol/everglade-previous-wire.md.

A previous wire (#13398): what a wire 7 room writes a seat whose hello said wire 6 or older, and reads from it (the familiar frames m1 to m8 and M1 M3 to M7, and the kit's U1 and u1, in place of the rows, E kinds and e entries of #13276). Kept until production's page speaks wire 7 (WIRE_LIVE); a change that raises WIRE_VERSION adds a row beside it; docs/protocol/everglade-previous-wire.md.
Projectiles over a room: F (page to room), a and d (room to pages), pinned in the combat profile beside the creature frames (#13246); docs/protocol/everglade-projectiles-v1.md.

WebTransport framing: the mark byte and channel, 1,200-byte datagrams, and input datagrams that repeat the unacknowledged with the NET_SAME byte (#13176, #13246); docs/protocol/aethyr-transport-v1.md.
The optional latency observation frame @1.
Orbit League's session frames.

Seat ticket v5 (#13260): signed by the API's private key (BIP-340), checked by rooms with public keys only. The API calls the codec through coax/web/api/ticket-sign-unit.c; rooms through room-ticket.coax tk_check_keys.

Seat ticket HMAC v2, v3 and v4 (#13248): written by metaverse-engine/session/seat-ticket.coax seat_ticket_hmac_write (the API calls it) and checked by coax/web/room/room-ticket.coax tk_check, whose signers for dev rooms and checks (tk_sign and the rest) all call seat_ticket_hmac_write. The v4 envelope (resume_ticket_wrap, metaverse-engine/session/resume-envelope.coax) is pinned here too: the fixture's v4 ticket with its durable capture.

What a room shard and the API say to each other outside the session wire (E7 and E8, #13250): the vitals post and its receipt, the directory post, a drain's signed text, the control ask and the lines of its answer, and the checkpoint's receipt. The room writes and reads them through this file, its local stand-in for the API answers with it, and the API writes both receipts through it (coax/web/api/ticket-sign.coax). The API reads both posts through this file too (the vitals post's head and lines in player.c, the directory post's shard, endpoint and health lines in rooms.c, through coax/web/api/ticket-sign.coax); the readers take from every text what C's sscanf and atoi took before, and only SQL still builds the control answer. The fixture holds posts a room wrote and receipts and control answers a running API gave. docs/protocol/room-reports-v1.md.
Durable character resume profile 2 (ingress with sent and stored without sent; #13244).

The Character aggregate (#13290, AAA P4.1; docs/protocol/everglade-character-v1.md): class, XP, the floor level, known abilities, the ledger's bag and version by item ID, equipment, coin and quests, the record the server owns for each character. character.coax writes and reads it and owns its rules (char_level, char_class_set, char_fits, char_accept).

The Character aggregate's v2 (#13519; docs/protocol/everglade-character-v2.md): v1 and the Archery Range's lasting tally (range, 61 whole numbers: the best run, then each way of shooting's and band's shots, hits, points and golds), added to by an arrow's claim and cleared by RESET's. A record with no tally is written as v1, byte for byte; v1 reads as v2 with an empty tally (the upgrade). character.coax writes and reads both.

Content tables v1 (#13294, AAA P4.5; docs/protocol/aethyr-content-v1.md): a game's data as versioned tables of rows in one text document, which a room loads at start and Aethyrforge edits on its edit log. tables.coax reads and writes it and refuses a dangling ID, a place out of reach, a sum that is wrong and any bytes but the document's one form. Everglade's tables (creatures, spawns, abilities, items, loot, quests, dialogue, points) are everglade/content/everglade.content, bound by everglade/model/content.coax.

A room's ledger operation and the store's answer (#13291, AAA P4.2; docs/protocol/everglade-item-op-v1.md): loot, quest stages and rewards, and what a character wears, each one operation with an ID (read, grant, consume, claim) and a claim on the character's record applied with it once; the answer is the ledger's status and the character as the store has it (the record, the kinds of its bag, the inventory version). The room posts it to POST /api/playtest/room-items under room-write purpose items; player.c answers through io_answer. The ledger's rules are metaverse-engine/session/ledger.coax's and the record's are everglade/model/character.coax's.

Domain event (#13319, DDD.8): an item was granted to a character. Published by the item ledger's outbox in the grant's transaction (verse.item_outbox, op grant; LedgerEntry in metaverse-engine/session/ledger.coax); a reader takes rows after the last sequence it took (verse.item_outbox_since). Typed IDs only: the sequence, the character, the item, its content kind, the time.

Domain event (#13319, DDD.8): a character's level rose. Published by the characters' outbox (verse.character_outbox, migration 0176) in the transaction that changes the record (player.c character_outbox: a seat ticket, an accepted checkpoint, a ledger operation's XP claim); events.coax ev_levelled decides. A reader takes rows after the last sequence it took (verse.character_outbox_since).
Diagnostic code 1 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link state, retry no. Nothing in the realm's state or content has this id. Fix the id, or author the thing.
Diagnostic code 2 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link spawned, retry yes. It is in the state, and the world builds it at its next commit. Ask again after a frame.
Diagnostic code 3 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link spawned, retry no. The world had no free slot for it. Remove something or raise the world's capacity.
Diagnostic code 4 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link spawned, retry no. It was in the world and was removed: defeated, opened or deleted. It comes back only by a reset or an edit.
Diagnostic code 5 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link view, retry no. It stands outside what the camera sees. Move or turn the camera.
Diagnostic code 6 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link drawn, retry yes. Its draw rows are older than the state. The next frame writes them.
Diagnostic code 7 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link drawn, retry no. The draw list or its store was full, and it was left out. Draw fewer things or raise the limit.
Diagnostic code 8 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link drawn, retry no. The realm or its host hides it now: a mode that doesn't show it, or a host that draws this kind itself.
Diagnostic code 9 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link asset, retry yes. Its mesh, texture or pack is still arriving.
Diagnostic code 10 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link asset, retry no. Its asset was fetched and refused, or the fetch failed.
Diagnostic code 11 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link asset, retry no. Its kind names no asset.
Diagnostic code 12 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link collider, retry no. It should block or be touched, and has no collider.
Diagnostic code 13 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link collider, retry no. It has a collider that doesn't block now.
Diagnostic code 14 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link system, retry yes. The system that moves it hasn't run since it spawned.
Diagnostic code 15 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link system, retry no. The system that moves it is stopped: a mode, a pause or a budget.
Diagnostic code 16 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link runtime, retry no. A budget was reached and work was dropped. The line names the limit and how much was dropped.
Diagnostic code 17 (#13429, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): link runtime, retry no. A pack was read and refused.

Realm frame messages v1 (#13432, docs/metaverse/realm-origin.md): what the site's page and a realm in its sandboxed frame post to each other (window.postMessage): hello and ask from the site, ready, answer and refused from the realm. A realm that runs someone else's code is served from the realm origin with no origin of its own, and these are the only words between the two. The browser glue (coax/web/realm-frame.js, host.js coaxial.framed) carries the text and judges nothing; a realm's module reads and writes it through the codec (Splice: splice_framed).
Durable character resume profile 3 (adds rest and optional uses; #13244).
Room writes v1 (#13260): each shard signs its writes to the API with its own key, the shard and purpose inside the signed bytes; the API checks through ticket-sign-unit.c (rooms.c room_write_signed).

Content numbers (#13286): the number a wire frame or a save carries for an ability (a cast's SLOT in C and e cast), a spell (an event's SPELL), a creature template (a stat block), an item kind and a spawn (h2 and h3's M), each frozen under a key. The registry is the codec; class-kit.coax (xk_wire), creatures.coax (E2M_SPAWN) and the rules' tables are held to it by their checks. wire-check rule 7 fails on a row of the base's copy that is gone or changed. The P frame's content pin is sealed with the table's hash (everglade-wire.coax WIRE_CONTENT_IDS); docs/protocol/everglade-content-ids-v1.md.

Moderation v1 (#13302): a moderator's record (VERB PID MINUTES REASON), a room's command (X and the record), its report to the API (POST /api/playtest/room-mod-log, room-write purpose moderation) and receipt, and the room's answer to the moderator (q). The rules live in the codec file too. The API calls it through coax/web/api/moderation-policy.coax (player.c, room.c).

Crash report v1 (#13298, docs/deployment/crash-reports.md): what a room shard posts to POST /api/playtest/room-crash after a crash (signed as its room-write `crash` purpose), and what the API builds from a page's crash event. room-crash.coax builds a room's report from its handler's dump (room-crash.c) and addr2line's names, builds a page's, and checks and reads both; the API calls it through ticket-sign-unit.c and stores the body whole, by the md5 of its source and sig line.

Crash report v2 (#13379, docs/deployment/crash-reports.md): a page's report whose frames carry their code offsets, `f NAME +0xOFFSET`, so a frame resolves to a Coax line after the fact. The API builds it from a page's crash event (host.js sends each frame as NAME and its offset) and reads v1 and v2; the signature and the bucket are v1's. A room's report stays v1.

Crash report v3 (#13379, docs/deployment/crash-reports.md): a native app's crash. The iPhone and Mac apps write a dump from MetricKit's crash diagnostic (CrashReports.swift: `appdump 1` and its lines, in the schema) and post it to POST /api/playtest/app-crash; room-crash.coax makes the report from it (crash_app_report), and the API keeps it by bucket. A frame is `f BINARY +0xOFFSET`; the build line is the app binary's UUID, which names its dSYM.

Capacity record v1 (#13296, docs/deployment/soak.md): one night's soak of the full fleet. soak.coax writes it through soak-record.coax and posts it to POST /api/playtest/capacity-record (signed as a room's `capacity` write); the API checks it and reads its day, environment, seats and verdict through the same codec (ticket-sign-unit.c), stores the body whole, one a day and environment, and GET /api/playtest/capacity answers the newest as it was kept. The status page reads its lines.

A world's edits v1 (#13412, the browser editor's E3; docs/protocol/world-edit-v1.md): one typed edit (spawn, despawn, set a column, move, rotate, scale, set a content cell, shape the land) and the batch that names the revision it was made from (apply, undo, redo, original, publish-now, publish-next). world-edit.coax writes and reads both and carries an entity edit out on the engine's edit log with its inverse. POST /api/worlds/ID takes a batch (worlds.c reads its head through world-policy.coax); a world's own Coax carries it out (Splice: metaverse/splice-bots/world.coax).

What /api/worlds/ID answers (#13412): a lane's revision, the dev and live revisions, when live's last update reaches sessions, the undo log's steps, and the lane's document (a read) or the batch as it was taken (a write); or a refusal in words naming the edit refused. Pinned in the edit profile beside the batch.

A world's document v1 (#13412; docs/protocol/world-doc-v1.md): the World saved whole (entities, every column, the realm's own columns), the content revision, the edit log's head and the next entity number, with a digest. world-doc.coax writes it (world_save) and loads it (world_load), refusing a document that does not give its own digest. The API stores it as text (verse.world_docs, migration 0181) and carries it unread; Splice's is the game's World (metaverse/splice-bots/world.coax).

Domain event (#13412): an edit to a world was saved. Published by the realm-authoring outbox (verse.world_outbox, lane dev, migration 0181) in the transaction that changes the document, one event a revision; a reader takes the event whose revision is one above the last it took (we_take). Typed fields only: the sequence, the world, the revision, the edit, the time.

Domain event (#13412): a world's dev revision became live. Published by the same outbox on the live lane, with the dev revision it was made from, when it reaches open sessions (now or next) and the pins of the build that reads it (engine, rules, content, wire); metaverse-engine/editor/world-live.coax decides what a session does with it.

One result for every realm operation (#13436; docs/protocol/realm-result-v1.md): done with the new revision, running, needs approval, a dry run with its level, refused with a code and whether a retry can help, or unknown. Every result names the realm, the revision, the build and the page it touched (#13437). The CLI's realm commands answer it (--json: the report's "result"), the realm_* MCP tools carry it, and coax drive prints it for a world's edits.

What an engine page tells the editor shell that ?edit opens over it (#13416; docs/protocol/editor-model-v1.md): the world, its lane and revision, what can be undone and redone, the selection, the columns an edit may set, the kinds, the entities and the last refusal. The realm writes it, the shell reads it, and it never leaves the page. A realm's world adds its visitors' proposals waiting for the owner as `card` and `from` lines (#13527): the realm's page writes them from the proposals it reads, and the shell tells them to the conversation in its foot. A realm's world adds its asks too (`asks`, `q`; #13528), for the conversation's realm tools.

A realm script's manifest (#13467; docs/protocol/realm-script-v1.md): what a script module is and may do, as one line of JSON in one form. Its hash, size, memory, state, handlers, powers and calls are facts of the bytes, read from the module the check passed (metaverse-engine/script/wasm.coax), never from what an author sent. The name and the state fields are the author's.

A world's script status (#13467; docs/protocol/realm-script-v1.md): one line of JSON for the editor's script pane and coax drive. For each loaded script: its place, name and hash, whether it is switched off, how many things it drives, its calls and failures, the instructions it spent this tick and the most one call has spent, and its last diagnostic by id; with the call and tick budgets.

A script frame (#13467; docs/protocol/realm-script-v1.md): what a realm hands the script host for one tick, as fixed little-endian rows after the magic SFR1: the things a script may see, the events, the time and a seed. The page passes it to its script module as bytes and a room passes the same bytes to the host it links.

A script tick's result (#13467; docs/protocol/realm-script-v1.md): the commands a realm applies to its own running state and the diagnostics it shows, as fixed little-endian rows after the magic SRS1, with the instruction budget left and the calls made and failed.
Realm-script diagnostic code 1 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): A handler call spent its instruction budget and was undone.
Realm-script diagnostic code 2 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The script's module trapped and the call was undone; the line is the script's source line when it knows it.
Realm-script diagnostic code 3 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): A write or an engine call named a thing other than the one the handler was called for; the call was undone.
Realm-script diagnostic code 4 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The tick's command list was full; the call was undone.
Realm-script diagnostic code 5 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The world's instruction budget for the tick was spent; the script's remaining calls were skipped.
Realm-script diagnostic code 6 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The script failed several calls in a row and is off until it is loaded again.
Realm-script diagnostic code 7 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): A number that is not finite, or a slot, timer or point that does not exist; the call was undone.
Realm-script diagnostic code 8 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The module check refused the bytes; the detail is the refusal and the line the byte.
Realm-script diagnostic code 9 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): More things use the script than it has state slots.
Realm-script diagnostic code 10 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The module's face answered out of range.

A world's stored scripts (#13467; docs/protocol/world-scripts-v1.md): the limits a server states (scripts a world, a module's bytes, stored modules, the instruction budgets, an author's uploads and compiles a day, an account's reports a day, whether this server compiles a source), then each stored script's manifest (realm.script.v1, the bytes the server wrote from the checked module), whether it is switched off and why, and whether its source is kept; ascending by hash, compact, one form. GET /api/worlds/ID/scripts answers it (scripts.c through script-store.coax); a page and a room read it to skip a script that is off.

A script route's refusal (#13467; docs/protocol/world-scripts-v1.md): a diagnostic code, whether a retry can help, the words, a refused module's refusal name and byte, the limit that was reached and when it lifts, and what a publish asks the publisher to confirm (each new or growing script by hash, with the handlers, powers and calls it adds). The script routes answer it, and POST /api/worlds/ID answers it for a publish that needs a confirmation (409).

The open reports of scripts, for an admin (#13467; docs/protocol/world-scripts-v1.md): each with its number, world, the module's hash, who reported, why, when and its status (open, kept, removed). GET /api/admin/scripts/reports answers it.
What a report, a switch-off, a switch-on or a keep did (#13467; docs/protocol/world-scripts-v1.md): which, and the module's hash.
Stored-script refusal code 3 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The world has stored no module of this hash.
Stored-script refusal code 4 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The module is switched off everywhere: it is not served and no new edit names it.
Stored-script refusal code 5 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): A publish adds a script or lets one do more; nothing was published until the publisher confirms each by hash.
Stored-script refusal code 6 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The world stores as many modules as it may.
Stored-script refusal code 7 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The author's daily limit is spent; the answer says the limit and when it lifts.
Stored-script refusal code 8 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): This server compiles no source.
Stored-script refusal code 9 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The compile job refused the source; the words are the compiler's or the job's.
Stored-script refusal code 10 (#13467, proto/README.md "Diagnostic codes"): The request is not one the route takes.

A realm's code from the browser, on the dev server only (#13421; docs/protocol/realm-code-v1.md): the editor shell asks coax serve for the realm's own source files, one file's text, or a save, and a save is answered with the compiler's check. Only serve.c while it watches answers POST /coaxial/code; --static, the API and the realm origin have no such route, and a path that is not the page's own realm source is refused.

A world's imported assets as the editor's asset browser lists them and as an import answers (#13420; docs/protocol/world-assets-v1.md): the import pack's SHA-256 and size, the limits shown before a file is sent, the licences an import may declare, each asset with the file it came from, and what the last import did. The route that packs an import writes it (the dev server's tool and the API, both through metaverse/splice-bots/world-assets.coax); the editor shell reads it.

An import's body (#13420): a line that names the licence, by its number, and the file as it was dropped, then the file's bytes as they are. The editor shell writes the line; the page's host sends it with the file (coax/web/dom-host.js, dom_file_send); the route that packs the import reads it.

A file named by its content before it is sent (#13420; docs/protocol/world-assets-v1.md): where a world's server takes a file by direct upload (the API), the ask is the licence, the file's bytes and name, and its SHA-256; the answer says where exactly that many bytes go (an upload the API opened in its private bucket) or that storage has the file. The same ask says the upload is done, and the API then reads the object back, checks it against its name and imports it. The editor shell writes the ask and the page's host adds the hash (coax/web/dom-host.js, dom_file_step).

The attachments on a project and its worlds (#13468; docs/protocol/world-files-v1.md): the world, its project, what the project holds and the limits, then each attachment with its scope, kind, size, hash, name, link, note and tags, and what the last write did. The dev server's store and the API write it; the editor's Files pane, the realm commands and the agent read it. It never reaches a player or a pack.
(#13468; docs/protocol/world-files-v1.md) A file attached whole or in parts: its scope, size, the byte its part starts at and its name, then its note, tags and SHA-256, then the bytes.
